newsitem.title: ITALY: Space insurers to see Sealaunch system.
newsitem.headline: Space insurers to see Sealaunch system.

text.p: Space insurers will be invited to Glasgow's Clydeside in September to assess the development of a system to launch space rockets from oil-rig style platforms.
The invitation was given by Walter Lewis, vice president of Sealaunch Company Ltd, at the Generali space insurance conference in Venice on Thursday.
Sealaunch is a joint venture between U.S. aerospace giant Boeing, shipbuilder Kvaerner and two Russian rocket firms.
Lewis said insurers would be invited to inspect the command ship being built at Govan shipyard as part of its campaign to convince insurers that the innovative Sealaunch plan will work.
The company has converted an oil rig into a platform which can launch Zenith rockets equipped with RD171 engines from a semi-submerged position in international waters near the equator.
Rockets and payloads will be put together in a giant hangar on the command ship and transferred to the platform.
The ship will then move to a five kilometre safety distance and control fuelling and launch operations via umbilical connections.
Lewis said the first launch will take place in 1998.
